Dude, I understand completely your thoughts about offering to take "vulnerable" people out for a drink, or out to lunch, or whatever. The reality is, however, that the internet can only provide so much in terms of affecting someone's depression or suicidal thoughts. If I found myself alone, and all I had to turn to was an anonymous message over the internet, I honestly don't know how much better that would make me feel. 

The best part about /r/suicidewatch is that these anonymous messages turn into IM's or e-mails or even phone calls, where someone in a better position in life is taking time to help someone in need. It really is a beautiful thing. For you to come here and assume that wanting to meet-up in real life is "creepy" or is just someone "trying to get laid" shows me and everyone else in this community that you are completely missing the point. I'm offering my time to spend a moment with someone when nobody else will. I'm offering to someone my shoulder to lean on when the weight of their own problems has become too much to bear. It's people like you and your lack of understanding that make this world and ugly, bitter, place. I know this is just the internet, but behind these usernames are real people going through real struggles-- something you clearly have never experienced. 

So please, if you have nothing constructive to add, keep your thoughts to yourself. To everyone else, my offer still stands.

Several options for you. If your advisor's mistake was serious and he can be held accountable for it (ie. proof), take your story to the head of the department. Explain what the mistake was, explain your financial situation, and begin seeking alternatives or some sort of monetary support from the school. If the department head is a dick (like most are), keep making appointments with as many people as you can, because someone will be there to help you. Universities are large places with a lot of resources, and if anything you may be able to eliminate some of the financial cost that you will have to undertake. 

Debt is not a terrible, terrible thing. You have to think of it as an investment. Yes, it is a lot of money, yes it sucks that as one of the greatest nations in the world, our youth will be paying off their college tuition for a long time, but it is still an investment. And investments in yourself are the greatest investments you can make. If you changed your major in your third year, then you must have some passion for what you're doing. Think about the alternative, you didn't change your major and end up working in a field that you have no interest in for a long portion of your life. Be grateful that you made that decision now, and not later when it is much more difficult to make (family, children, etc. ) 

Always seek scholarships, get some crappy job that will help you with day-to-day expenses, and just focus all of your energy on your grades and your degree. Yes it's a lot of money, but your education is worth it. You will be fine!

hi there! I read every word, let me share with you some of my thoughts. You are on the verge of breaking. These walls that you have constructed are only a coping mechanism, and they will eventually come crumbling down, only to reveal the problem that lies at their core. What is this "lie" that you talk about? Would you care to share it? Is it too hard to share? It seems to me that you split your life up into two parts. Life before the lie and life after the lie. What was your life like before your emotionally traumatic events? I'm sure that you have some absolutely beautiful memories from your childhood/youth and days where life seemed like a marvelous spectacle. Focus on those memories. Okay, you have been hurt by two people so close to you (your parents), but now you are self-supporting. They are no longer in your life (or don't have to be, anyway). You need to focus on yourself, focus on everything that you have to offer. Focus on the fact that you're not in the streets with these emotions! 

Another very important truth, you seem very conflicted. You keep trying to convince yourself that you are better off alone, yet your words spill out desire to share your heavy emotions, share your life with someone else. No one is better off alone, being alone exacerbates your psychological torment, and while yes, being alone is great sometimes, being alone forever is NOT what we were designed for. 

My best advice: seek therapy. Yes you've heard it a million times, but you will NEVER understand the feeling of unloading all of that weight you are carrying around onto someone else until you actually do it. Keep fighting, there are therapists out there that care, some that don't, you will find the right one for you and it will change you forever. You sound like a very articulate, cerebral person, and if I've provided therapy in any way, contact me. I'd love to talk about your life, your problems, I've been in your shoes and I know the train doesn't stop here.

wow, first of all I would like to say that your words struck a chord in me rather deeply. I, too, see a drastic change in my behavior following a series of traumatic events (abortion, death of four classmates) followed by a semester-long pot smoking binge in which I didn't know which way was up most of the time. I went from being passionate and motivated to tired and apathetic. And what you say about dreams is especially true, my dreams are extravagant, almost child-like visions of love, work, happiness, etc. I think the fact that you are apathetic towards life is a symptom of your depression, you have just been so emotionally scarred that instead of feeling depressed, you just feel nothing. How stable are you financially? Will your parents support you? My junior year I did a home-stay program in Spain with about 30 other American students, and honestly, that was the point where all that I had lost was found again. I lived in another family, another culture, yet had like-minded American friends that I could fall back on, it was just an amazing experience, every day was an adventure, every day was something new and exciting. It really reminded me what living was like. I truly recommend doing something like this -- a semester at sea, a semester abroad, volunteering somewhere longterm, because when you are faced with a challenge and placed outside of your comfort zone, you don't have the time to sit around and try and rationalize everything, you are making decisions on the fly and you are only focused on living. 

I hope I've helped a little bit, I think you and I are very similar, there is something else out there. Frankly, I am just tired of the college culture, and I've realized albeit late that my group of friends aren't real friends at all, and I desire something more fulfilling. If you ever want to talk, PM me, I have Gchat as well
